items.stem: A criticism of using return on investment (ROI) as a divisional performance measure is that it may:

options.text: Lead managers to reject projects that would benefit the group as a whole
options.rationale: Correct: ROI can cause dysfunctional rejection of good projects that lower the divisional ROI.

options.text: Always align divisional and group interests
options.rationale: ROI often causes goal incongruence, not perfect alignment.

options.text: Ignore the capital employed in a division
Be impossible to calculate from accounting data
options.rationale: ROI is readily computed from accounting data.

items.explanation: Correct: ROI can cause dysfunctional rejection of good projects that lower the divisional ROI.

options.text: An imputed interest charge on the capital employed

options.text: Total fixed costs of the group
options.rationale: RI does not deduct group-wide fixed costs.
Dividends are not deducted in computing RI.

items.stem: Select TWO limitations of relying solely on financial performance measures.

options.rationale: Correct: financial measures largely report past performance.
Correct: a short-term financial focus can harm long-term value.
Customer satisfaction is a non-financial measure.
Morale is a non-financial, qualitative measure.

options.text: They always predict future cash flows accurately
options.rationale: Financial measures do not reliably predict the future.
